about: Synthetic planning meeting for evaluating summaries (#70). Every name, place, and number is invented. It has no title, so it's named with the app's title code, and it states its purpose at the start. It plants: budget numbers, a self-corrected date, a decision with its reason, an open question, a rejected option, and tasks with owners and a conditional plan. Each expect entry lists accepted spellings separated by |.
notes:
- budget
- move date
- Harbor Street vs Elm Court
segments: Thanks everyone. Today we need to pick the new office and lock the move date.
Priyanka here. I visited both places last week, Harbor Street and Elm Court.
Harbor Street is forty-eight thousand dollars a year, Elm Court is fifty-five thousand.
What do we get for the extra seven thousand at Elm Court?
Mostly parking. Elm Court includes twelve parking spaces. Harbor Street has none, but it's two blocks from the train.
Jonah. Honestly, almost everyone takes the train now. In the survey only four people said they drive.
Then parking isn't worth seven thousand a year. Any other differences?
Harbor Street has one more meeting room, three instead of two. Elm Court is a bit bigger overall, about nine hundred square feet more.
We don't need the extra space with the hybrid schedule. I think Harbor Street is the right call.
Great, decision made. Now the date. When does our current lease end?
The lease ends on the thirtieth of November, so we have to be out by then.
Harbor Street can give us the keys on November fourteenth, no wait, sorry, it's the twenty-first. The fourteenth was the other building.
So keys on the twenty-first and out by the thirtieth. That's nine days. Tight, but doable.
Priyanka. The movers I talked to want two weeks' notice, and they quoted three thousand two hundred dollars for a weekend move.
Let's plan the move for the weekend of the twenty-second and twenty-third, then.
Works for me. I'll book the movers this week so we stay inside their two weeks.
What about internet? Last time that took forever.
Jonah. The building's provider needs ten business days to install fiber. If I order it Monday, it should be in by the twentieth.
And if it's not ready by the twenty-first?
Then we use the hotspots for a few days. We have six of them in the storage room.
Okay. One open question, do we keep the old desks or buy new ones?
Nobody knows yet. Facilities is checking whether the old desks even fit the new layout. They'll tell us by next Wednesday.
Let's leave that open until Wednesday then.
So, to recap. Harbor Street, forty-eight thousand a year. Keys on the twenty-first, move the weekend of the twenty-second.
Priyanka books the movers this week. Jonah orders the fiber on Monday, and if it's late we fall back to the hotspots.
And I'll sign the Harbor Street lease by Friday. Desks wait for facilities on Wednesday.
